This chain of indications implies a potential role for Fluorouracil in the pathogenesis of gastric neoplasms, possibly through its anti-proliferative effects on gastric epithelial cells. The presence of a clinically established indication for Fluorouracil in gastric conditions, combined with the indirect evidence of its involvement in the progression of gastric neoplasms, supports the hypothesis that Fluorouracil may exert a mechanistic effect on gastric neoplasms. The integration of these pathways suggests that Fluorouracil could be a candidate for repurposing in the treatment of gastric neoplasms, though further experimental validation is required to confirm its direct mechanism of action.
